name: Starting Shelf Island

views.label: Detail 5: The door and its rock pillars
Detail 10: Rock pillars on the cliff

desc: a floating shelf of dark rock 40 m wide and 56 m long with a ragged asymmetric outline, about 6 m thick at the rim and tapering into an inverted cone 48 m deep with a faint bronze vein glowing inside it, six thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings into the haze. At the near end is the SPAWN TERRACE, an irregular paved patch about 13 x 9 m of cracked slabs of different sizes, with a shallow bronze arrival disc (3.6 m across, three concentric rings, slightly sunken and cracked) at its centre and a low broken rock lip behind it; a tiny plain 1.8 m human silhouette stands on the disc facing the door in every view for scale. A broken road of uneven worn slabs about 4 m wide, with a thin broken bronze inlay line, leads about 11 m to THE BEAM: one colossal weathered bronze I-girder 16 m long with a 2.5 m wide top, lying slightly crooked (about 15 degrees off the straight line) across a ragged meandering crack that cuts the whole island from rim to rim, 8 to 11 m wide with stepped broken lips and a 60 m drop into haze; the beam is level but dented, rust-streaked, matte, dusty, with missing rivets and a chipped corner, never polished. Beyond it a broken irregular forecourt about 13 x 4 m, then three worn uneven steps rising to THE DOOR, shown LOCKED, cut into the face of a huge black rock cliff with raw rock on both sides: 8 m high, carved stone frame 7.6 m wide with a crown of bronze finials, battered green-bronze verdigris scrollwork leaves dark with soot, two thick rusted chains wound across both leaves held by one huge closed padlock, a thin bright amber line of light through the centre gap, exactly like the Core Fantasy key-art door. Behind the door the cliff holds a walkable antechamber: a 3 m passage, then an irregular carved hall about 16 x 11.5 m with an 11 m cracked ceiling, four stout columns (two whole, two broken) around a clear aisle, a low round dais 4.5 m across where three weapons hover, completely dark inside with no daylight (only the faint glow of the weapons), a small west alcove, and, at the east side of the hall, a short flight of 5 wide worn stone steps going DOWN into a 4 m opening (the exit tunnel) in the east wall that leads out onto a rock ledge on the cliffs east face where a fixed bridge leaves toward the next island. The door sits low at the foot of ONE enormous, deep, solid mountain of black-brown fractured rock that rises 36 m at its west shoulder and 60 m at its summit, as thick and heavy as it is tall, with a huge cave carved inside it. The whole mass is built from countless big rough boulders, slabs, ribs and buttresses piled and jammed together, so the area around the door is crowded with many large rocks and ledges, with broken scree at their feet. Its upper part splits into two high crooked peaks (60 m and a 36 m one leaning west), which are simply the top of the same mass, not separate objects. All one rock: NO windows, NO openings, NO bricks or cut stone, NO tiers, NO battlements, NO carvings, nothing built. Only a faint amber glow deep in a few natural cracks. Around the base stand six chunky broken rock outcrops of 20 to 48 m, different heights, thick at the base, blunt snapped tops, NOT needles, NOT cones, NOT icicles. NO masonry on them: no bricks or courses of cut stone, no battlements, no crenellations, no arched windows, no columns, no domes, no bands or carved panels, nothing that looks built, Roman or medieval. Three bare dead trees (6 m, 4.5 m, and a 2.8 m broken stump) stand off the road, a few small uneven clumps of dry grass, and rubble in uneven scatters of different-sized stones; no mirror symmetry anywhere, immense, silent and ominous; match the attached approved ENV-01 hero image and blueprint sheets exactly, and add no second floating island or extra rock in the background
short: Crooked ravine, weathered beam, locked door in a cliff, walkable antechamber

name: Small Stepping Island
desc: a single heavy spire of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, thick and rough, built from big broken rock slabs that wind around its core like a slow whirlwind, with only thin lighter brown seams between the slabs, a few rough black rock fins sticking out of the sides, one small flat round top with room for a few steps and a long rough tapering tail underneath with a faint bronze vein glowing deep in the cracks and a few small hanging rock shards. One weathered bronze ring band, dented and green with verdigris, is wrapped around its waist. On the flat top, on the west edge, a short fixed stone bridge arrives and ends at a small bronze anchor socket set in the rock; on the east edge, a thin plank-and-chain bridge leaves from a second small bronze anchor socket. One thick rusted chain hangs from a bronze rim ring on the pad edge into the haze. One bare dead tree and a few small clumps of dry grass grow on the top. The top is cracked slabs of different sizes with loose chips. Everything is natural rock except the two bridge ends, the two anchor sockets, the chain and the bronze ring. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. No buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches
short: Twisted whirlwind spire with a bronze ring

name: Medium Island with Windbreak
desc: a medium floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 30 m wide, with a ragged uneven outline and a heavy rough underside. Along its north edge rises ONE GRAND MASSIF of natural rock: huge, thick and monumental, like a small mountain range or the great rock buttes of a canyon land, and like the tall rock clusters in the approved key art. It is a single mass that grows out of the island with no gaps at its base. It has a very wide heavy base about 22 m wide, and out of it rise five or six enormous crags of very different heights. TOWERING is the point. The crags are like the great spires of the Dolomites, the basalt pillars of Zhangjiajie and the fractured slate peaks of a mountain range, only crooked and leaning. THE BIGGEST CRAG RISES ABOUT TWICE AS HIGH AS THE WHOLE ISLAND IS WIDE (about 55 m on a 30 m island), so in the front view it is far taller than the island is long, and the island looks small beneath it. The second crag is about 38 m, then 34 m, 26 m, 18 m and 12 m, so the skyline is a jagged crown of very different heights: one extra tall spire, two or three tall ones, then medium ones and low broken shoulders. Do NOT make them all the same height. Every crag is thick at the base and rises in a long tapering shape, narrowing unevenly toward a ragged broken top, with long vertical fluting and deep vertical cracks, big ledges, overhangs and collapsed notches, wind grooves and thin lighter brown seams. They stand as ONE TIGHT OVERLAPPING CLUSTER, NOT in a fan, NOT in a row, NOT side by side like the fingers of a hand: some crags in front, some behind, two leaning against each other, one leaning out over the hollow, each leaning 10 to 25 degrees at a different angle, tops broken and jagged, the tallest off to the left of centre. They are fused at the base into one wide heavy mass with lower rock buttresses and stepped shoulders, with a few fallen boulders at the foot. They are NOT short blunt boulders, NOT squat blocks, NOT thin slabs, NOT planks, NOT fins, NOT ribs, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT a neat row of equal stones, NOT like fingers, and NOT icicles or cones. In front of the crags the top dips into a small sheltered hollow with a plain flat floor of bare dark rock with nothing lying on it, thin straight bronze lines inlaid in the floor leading to one short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There are no steps, no stairs and no platforms. On the west edge a thin plank-and-chain bridge arrives at a short bronze socket post, and on the east edge a short fixed stone bridge end with a second short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. The posts are plain short bronze posts. The underside tapers to a rough cone with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. At the south-east edge, away from the crags, a big flat-topped natural boulder with a worn smooth top sits right on the rim, facing the open sky. Nobody sits on it. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no extra bowls, no grass, no stumps, no rubble on the floor, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches, no stairs
short: A crooked crest of tall and extra tall rock spires shelters a quiet hollow with the first ignition column

name: Large Plateau Island
desc: a large floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 60 m wide, with sheer broken cliff faces all around, a ragged oval outline, and a deep underside like an upside-down mountain of fractured rock with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. In the middle of the top is one DEEP CRATER, about 30 m across and 18 m deep, with sheer cracked rock walls and three broad broken ledges stepping down to a flat floor far below. The crater is an irregular oval, NOT round, NOT neat rings, NOT a stadium, NOT a quarry with tidy steps. Thin amber light glows faintly in the cracks of the crater floor and walls, dim and dormant, like a sleeping reservoir of energy. Thin straight bronze lines are inlaid in the crater floor. Around the crater rim stand six huge NATURAL ROCK SPIRES of very different heights, scattered at different distances, some close together in pairs and some alone, NOT in a row, NOT in a fan, NOT like fingers. The two biggest stand at the east edge and lean toward each other with a narrow gap about 6 m wide between them, like a natural rock gate: the tallest is about as tall as the whole island is wide (about 55 m), the other about 44 m. The four others, along the north and south-east rims, are about 34 m, 28 m, 22 m and 16 m. Every spire is thick at the base, tapering, crooked, ragged, with deep vertical cracks, ledges and broken tops, each leaning at a different angle. They are like the giant natural rock spires in the approved key art, very grand, the island looks small beneath the tallest. They are NOT thin slabs, NOT fins, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT icicles or cones. At the west edge is a flat landing about 10 m wide with a low natural rock lip. From the landing three rough broken rock paths lead east: one along the north rim, one along the south rim, and one straight out toward the crater edge. On the east rim of the crater, near the gate, stands ONE short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There is exactly ONE column, no second one. Through the gap between the two big spires a short fixed stone bridge end with one short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no floating slabs, no extra bowls, no grass, no trees, no stumps, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches, no stairs, no tall structures of any kind
short: A deep glowing crater ringed by giant natural rock spires, three ways across, one ignition column and a natural rock gate

name: Long Causeway Island
desc: a very long, narrow, THIN floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 80 m long and only 10 m wide, about EIGHT TIMES AS LONG AS IT IS WIDE, like a long flat blade or a fallen mountain ridge. It is a thin slab, only about 8 m thick in the middle, tapering to a point at both ends, with sheer broken cliff sides and a shallow underside with a few long hanging rock tendrils at the east end. The west end is where the player arrives and the east end is where he leaves. The top is a clean, open, flat-ish back of cracked dark rock, about 10 m wide, rough and uneven, with sheer drops on both sides. You can see right along it from end to end. One thin, perfectly straight bronze line is inlaid down the exact middle of the top, running the whole length. Along both edges of the back stand HUGE NATURAL ROCK SPIRES, thick at the base, tapering, crooked, ragged, with sharp angular fractured faces, long vertical cracks and broken tops, exactly like the giant natural rock spires of the approved key art and like the two gate spires of the Large Plateau Island. They stand in leaning PAIRS, one on the north edge and one on the south edge, leaning toward each other ACROSS the walking back so that their tops almost touch, like the natural rock gate on the Large Plateau Island. In a row from west to east: a small pair about 16 m high near the west end; a bigger pair about 24 m high close beside it; then a long open gap; then a broken pair in the middle where the south spire stands about 20 m high and its partner on the north edge has snapped off to a jagged stump about 5 m high; then the TALLEST pair just east of the middle, about 34 m high (the tallest reaches almost half as high as the island is long) with a narrow gap of about 4 m between their tops; then one single low spire about 9 m high on the north edge near the east end. The heights are very different and the spacing is uneven. At the west end a short flat tongue of the same rock, with one short bronze post at its tip, reaches out toward the previous island, and at the east end a second short flat tongue of rock with one short bronze post reaches out toward the next place. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no boulders or rubble lying on the back, no grass, no trees, no stumps, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no stairs, no towers
short: A very long thin rock blade with pairs of giant natural spires leaning together across the path

views.label: Detail 5: Throne on the top terrace

desc: the tallest and by far the largest floating island, a huge tiered mountain peak of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 150 m wide and 90 m tall above a long tapering root of rock, rising far above every other island, ONE broad winding path of broken, uneven, irregular rock steps cut into the front of the mountain, five long flights zigzagging up the face from a low flat rock ledge at the west foot, joined by four flat landings at the turns, each flight wide enough for several people, with one thin bronze line down the middle of the path, near the top a wide flat open crown platform of cracked dark rock about 40 m across with ONE short stone column on a round bronze base in the middle and a faint ring of amber cracks around it, two tall natural rock spires leaning toward each other like a gate where the path reaches the crown (one very tall, one a little shorter), behind the crown a steep stair of broken dark rock steps, with six small bronze braziers (three on each side, dark and unlit), climbing to a higher broad flat terrace at the very top where the colossal Throne of Stillness, about 40 m tall, hewn from black volcanic stone: a deep massive seat block with two thick armrests facing south toward the stair, a very tall narrow monolith backrest with straight parallel sides and a flat notched top carrying six equally spaced horizontal amber fissures that glow only faintly, and two huge curved bronze dragon ribs rising on either side of it and arching inward like a cage stands, two huge natural rock spires of different heights flanking the foot of that rise (the tallest as tall as a quarter of the mountain), one lower single spire on the east edge of the crown, nothing else built, awe-inspiring, austere, golden haze, wreathed in cloud at the root. Dry and dead, no green

name: Canyon Cliffs
size: chain ~285 m long: five rock masses, four bridges and the Spine
desc: a chain of FIVE separate floating rock masses (two cliffs and three shelves) of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 285 m long in all, with wide gaps of open sky and a deep drop into cloud between them, loosely staggered and NOT in a straight row: a big West Cliff about 70 m long where the player arrives, a small South shelf south of the line, a Middle shelf south-east of it, a North shelf a little north of the line, and a huge East Cliff, the biggest, about 86 m long; the West Cliff and the East Cliff are the two halves of one split mountain, each with sheer vertical faces carrying the same five horizontal bands of thin lighter brown strata at the same heights, so the bands line up across the whole chain as though the mountain was torn apart; flat cracked broken tops; each mass hangs over a short thick tapering root of rough rock wreathed in cloud; three short bridges cross three of the gaps (West Cliff to South shelf, South shelf to Middle shelf, North shelf to East Cliff), each made of two heavy dark chains strung between two short bronze posts on a flat rock tongue at each side, with flat rungs of which only the first four at the near end glow amber-white; one narrow natural rock ridge as wide as a path joins the Middle shelf to the North shelf; one very long bridge of the same kind crosses from the West Cliff straight to the North shelf; ONE short stone column on a round bronze base on the East Cliff; a wide flat lip at the north-east corner of the East Cliff with faint heat shimmer rising and two low natural rock needles beside it; a cluster of three black natural rock needles of different heights on the north rim of the West Cliff; a round shallow hollow in the top of each of the West Cliff and the three shelves. Nothing is built. Dry and dead, no green

name: Twin Towers with Broken Arch
desc: two matching carved ruin towers of different heights, one with a cracked broken cap and one open-topped, joined near the top by a high stone arch bridge that is cracked and missing its middle section, gold-bronze bands, small amber-lit windows, grand and silent
short: Twin towers joined by a broken arch

name: Gatehouse Tower
desc: a broad fortress gatehouse tower with a huge pointed arch passage through its base, deep shadow inside, flanking carved guardian pilasters, empty bronze track grooves where a portcullis once hung, a stone crown of broken battlement teeth, weathered dark stone with gold-bronze trim, ruin not a city
short: Gatehouse with a huge arch passage

name: Long Rung Bridge
desc: a very long bridge made of two heavy dark chains with flat rungs, sagging slightly, anchored with bronze posts on a flat rock tongue at both ends, only the first four rungs at the near end glow amber-white and the rest are dark, the same make as the other canyon bridges, as in the Leap key art; fixed and rigid, not swaying
short: Long chain-and-rung bridge, first four rungs glowing

name: Leech Bridge Underside
size: 20 to 72 m long, fits the bridge
desc: the same long plank-and-chain bridge seen from slightly below, with four armored Ember Leeches clinging upside down to the underside planks and chains in the shadow, their tail sacs glowing a dull ember, one stretching up toward the walkway; dark, tense, mysterious
short: Leeches hanging under the bridge

name: Six-Line Floor Inlay
desc: a round paving plaza of cracked dark stone with six parallel straight bronze inlay bars set into the floor, glowing faintly amber, each bar a different length-matched element texture; shown dormant and lit
short: Six glowing bars inlaid in the floor

name: Fire Brazier, Standing
desc: a wide shallow bronze bowl on a short flared bronze stand sitting on the ground, burning with a steady lively flame and a few rising sparks, as the lone brazier in the Igara key art; weathered, ancient and simple
short: Standing bronze fire bowl

name: Rock-Spire Citadel Tower
desc: a very grand stacked tower: a leaning spire of dark rock with a tall narrow carved tower built up its side in many tiers, verdigris-bronze bands, arched windows with a faint amber glow, broken battlements at the top, smaller ruined towers clinging to the rock beside it, as in the Elias hero key art
short: Grand tiered tower on a rock spire

name: Obsidian Shard Cluster
desc: a leaning cluster of huge black obsidian blades with glassy edges and amber reflections, rising from tan rock, as the shard formations in the Igara key art
short: Leaning obsidian blade cluster

name: Dead Tree Grove
desc: a small group of three bare petrified dead trees with twisting branches and splintered roots gripping a rock slab, as in the Igara key art
short: Three dead trees on a rock slab

name: Bronze Door, Unlocked
desc: the same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame with bronze finials and battered verdigris scrollwork panels, now UNLOCKED: the huge padlock hangs open and the thick rusted chains have slid off and lie in heavy coils on the cracked paving, the two leaves still shut but a little loose, a brighter thin vertical amber light between them
short: The same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame

name: Bronze Door, Open
desc: the same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame with bronze finials, now OPEN: both battered verdigris leaves swung inward, the broken chains and open padlock lying on the paving, a deep stone antechamber beyond lit by warm gold-amber light pouring out across the floor, dust motes in the beams
short: The same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame

name: Six-Line Ladder, Dormant
desc: six very large straight horizontal beams of dark bronze with small end caps, stacked vertically with even spacing, parallel and equal in length, floating in the sky; shown dormant and unlit, each beam the size of a bridge; flat straight bars only, not a star shape, not a circle
short: Six very large straight horizontal beams of dark bronze

name: Six-Line Ladder, Progress States
desc: six equal straight horizontal glowing bars stacked vertically like the Interface key art, hot amber-white core, soft amber glow haze and a few embers drifting around them; show three versions side by side: bottom bar lit, bottom four lit, all six lit; unlit bars dark bronze; flat straight bars only
short: Six equal straight horizontal glowing bars stacked vertically like the Interface

name: Fire Eye, Open and Burning
desc: the Fire Eye, copy the attached Fire Eye reference exactly: a huge almond-shaped eye made of living fire, white-gold hot at the lid edge and deep orange-amber across the iris, the iris built from fine radial fibers like a sun, a narrow dark vertical diamond pupil, and the whole outline throwing out long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils into the sky like a solar corona; eye only, no face, no body; shown OPEN and burning
short: The Fire Eye, open and burning

name: Ringed Planet
desc: a very large ringed planet filling a big part of the sky, warm sepia and tan cloud bands, a thin pale ring crossing in front, bright rim halo on the sun side, as in the Fire Dragon and Interface key art
short: A very large ringed planet filling a big part of the sky

name: Plain Planet
desc: a large cratered brown-amber planet with a dark terminator shadow, no rings, soft rim glow, visible surface texture, as in the Fire Dragon key art
short: A large cratered brown-amber planet

name: Ember Planet
desc: a large dark planet cracked with glowing molten-orange fault lines like a cooling coal, a thin atmosphere halo of amber haze on one edge, no rings, hangs low on the horizon
short: Cracked molten ember planet

name: Fire Eye, Open and Dormant
desc: the same huge almond-shaped Fire Eye but with its fire out: the eye is carved from dark charcoal-bronze stone and cold metal, the iris a dull dim ember ring of radial fibers, the pupil a narrow dark vertical diamond, the outline a dead crown of long thin broken filaments like cooled lava glass, only a faint ember glow deep in the iris; eye only, no face
short: Open Eye, fire out

name: Fire Eye, Closed and Burning
desc: the same huge Fire Eye with the eyelids fully CLOSED: one smooth almond shape sealed shut by a single bright white-gold seam along the lid line, the closed lids glowing deep orange-amber, the long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils still streaming from the outline like a solar corona; no iris and no pupil visible; eye only, no face
short: Closed Eye, burning

name: Fire Eye, Closed and Dormant
desc: the same huge Fire Eye CLOSED and with its fire out: a sealed almond of dark charcoal-bronze stone with a hairline seam along the lid line, a faint dull ember glow only inside the seam, the outline filaments dark, cold and still; eye only, no face
short: Closed Eye, fire out

name: Six Lines, Six Elements (proposed)
desc: six equal straight horizontal bars stacked vertically with even spacing, each bar a different element yet the same size: bar one glowing embers and coal, bar two molten bronze, bar three spiralling wind and dust streaks, bar four crackling lightning, bar five flowing liquid fire, bar six pure white-gold light; all six clearly straight bars, all in the warm gold-amber palette
short: Six lines as six elements

name: The Throne of Stillness
desc: a colossal ancient throne hewn from black volcanic stone and aged bronze, about 40 m tall, unmistakably a throne: a deep massive seat block with two thick armrests, and rising far above it a very tall narrow monolith backrest with straight parallel sides and a flat top with ONE small rectangular notch in the middle, EXACTLY SIX short horizontal glowing amber bars (fissures) stacked at equal spacing up the front face of the backrest like a ladder of fire (count them: six), hot molten-amber cracks veining through the lower backrest and the stone like lava under a crust, on EACH side a cluster of THREE colossal curved tapering bronze ribs like dragon ribs or tusks (three on the left, three on the right, six in all) rising from the rock base and arching inward over the seat without touching, with molten fire glowing between them at their base, a short steep stair of broken black stone up the front to the seat with two small bronze braziers burning at the top corners and two at the foot of the stair, a rough broken rock plinth under everything, heavy rough weathered surfaces, thin embers rising
short: A colossal ancient throne hewn from black volcanic stone and aged bronze

name: The Throne Stairs and Platform
desc: the summit approach: a long steep staircase of broken black volcanic stone about 8 m wide, in two flights of about 25 steps with one flat landing between them, climbing 20 m, with two small bronze braziers burning on each side of the stair (four in all, in two pairs), leading up to a broad flat cracked stone terrace about 36 m across with thin molten-amber veins in the stone and a rough broken rim; nothing else on it, empty where the Throne will stand; heavy rough weathered surfaces
short: The summit approach: a long steep staircase of broken black volcanic stone about

name: Throne on Summit
desc: the colossal ancient volcanic-stone Throne of Stillness (very tall notched monolith backrest with EXACTLY SIX horizontal amber bars, on each side a cluster of three curved bronze ribs arching inward, six ribs in all) standing on the broad top terrace of the summit island above the clouds, the long steep staircase of broken black stone with four bronze braziers climbing up to the terrace from the flat crown below, the crown with its low column and two rock spires leaning together like a gate at its foot, jagged natural dark rock all around
short: The colossal ancient volcanic-stone Throne of Stillness (very tall notched monol

name: The Cinder (guide)
desc: a small floating faceted polyhedron fire construct about the size of a head, gold-bronze angular frame with glass-like triangular and hexagonal facets around a bright glowing ember core with a faint engraved symbol, no face, no limbs; shown LIT with a warm halo and a few drifting sparks (a second version DIM: core nearly out, frame cold, as in the Cinder key art)
short: A small floating faceted polyhedron fire construct about the size of a head

name: Fire Dragon
desc: a MASSIVE winged fire dragon matching the Fire Dragon key art: dark scaled body cracked with glowing amber-ember seams, huge membrane wings with ember-lit veins, spiked head ridge, long neck, jaws open breathing a long roaring stream of orange fire with sparks, long body and tail, shown flying; large enough to carry a rider on its shoulders
short: A MASSIVE winged fire dragon matching the Fire Dragon key art: dark scaled body

name: Glass Shadow
desc: a tall humanoid figure made of faceted transparent amber-gold glass crystal exactly as in the Glass Shadows key art, smooth faceless head, fine crack lines across the body, small glowing shards breaking off at one arm, a thin core of fire glowing inside the chest, drifting embers around the hands, symbolic force not a person
short: A tall humanoid figure made of faceted transparent amber-gold glass crystal exac

name: Burn Knight
desc: a heavy armored figure in dark matte black-bronze plate armor with amber-glowing visor and shoulder studs, a large round shield on one arm with a glowing swirling amber heat core and a ring of flame licking its rim, helmet without horns, small flames curling from the shoulders, symbolic force not a person
short: A heavy armored figure in dark matte black-bronze plate armor

name: Ember Leech
desc: a long armored centipede-like creature, dark segmented plates with thin glowing ember seams between segments, many thin legs, curved pincer tail with a glowing molten-ember sac at the rear, a few sparks dripping from it, clinging to a stone ledge or hanging upside down under a plank bridge
short: A long armored centipede-like creature

name: Storm Wraith (VFX reference)
desc: a large humanoid figure formed of dark swirling dust and storm cloud exactly as in the Storm Wraiths key art, long clawed hands, amber lightning veins running through it, flecks of fire in the swirl, no solid face, shown mid-stride
short: A large humanoid figure formed of dark swirling dust and storm cloud exactly as

name: Elias Suit Glow
desc: a rear three-quarter view of Elias, 21, short dark hair, matte obsidian bodysuit, whose circuit seams glow bright orange-amber, a soft aura of warm light and drifting embers around his whole body; shown at low glow and at full glow
short: Orange suit seams and aura

name: Sacred Arc
desc: a wide arc of golden fire and light sweeping through the air around Elias, thick glowing flame ribbon with a hot white-gold core and trailing sparks, as in the Sacred Arc key art
short: Golden fire arc

name: Stillness Rings
desc: concentric rings of orange light expanding from Elias standing still on the ground, thin hot circles with fine ember dust lifting inside them, calm and powerful, as in the Stillness Wins key art
short: Expanding stillness rings

name: Run Sparks
desc: a trail of fire sparks and ember streaks kicked up behind Elias as he runs, small bright points streaming back along his path, as in the Flow Over Force key art
short: Sparks kicked up while running

name: Ambient Ember Sparks
desc: slow floating fire sparks and glowing embers drifting upward in warm dusty air, varied sizes, some larger glowing flakes, used around Elias and across the islands
short: Drifting embers

name: Combat Flame Ring
desc: a controlled ring of orange flame circling Elias at waist height, a bright thin hot core with soft licking tongues of fire, restraint not chaos, as in the Combat Restraint key art
short: Controlled ring of flame

name: Hidden-System Energy Orbs
desc: floating glowing orbs of amber light connected by thin bright energy threads in a loose lattice, some orbs bright and some dim, as in the Hidden System key art
short: Orbs joined by energy threads

name: Dragon Fire Breath
desc: a long roaring jet of orange fire with a white-gold core streaming from a dragon jaw outline, swirling smoke and embers, hot and powerful
short: Fire stream from the dragon

name: Ring of Fire, Dormant and Ignited
desc: a vast circle of embers: shown dormant as a faint ring of dull glowing coals along a distant horizon, and ignited as a towering wall of fire with leaping flames and sparks, proposed final-world boundary
short: World-edge ring, dormant and lit
